ac992cc25d49.text: llm 0.37.2. Release: llm 0.37.2 Fixes a security issue reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w . LLM has a mechanism called extra-openai-models.yaml - now managed by the new-in-0.37 llm openai endpoint add command - for using LLM with OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. Daniel reported two ways this could accidentally send your configured OpenAI API key to one of those providers: if the key named by api_key_name had never been stored, or if a responses: true model was run with -o chat_completions 1 . adb66fa1efb1.text: The Jev Revolution: What Engineers Are Already Building with System One Models. Today at the AI Engineer Code Summit , the main theme was system one models — non-generative models that return structured choices, scores, or probabilities. They’re also typically much faster and cheaper than reasoning LLMs (a.k.a. system two models). And who better to give an inspirational rallying cry for system one models than Diogo Almeida , co-founder and CEO of TypeSafe AI . Almeida was lead creator of Jev , the product that kicked off this trend less than two months ago. Jev was an instant revelation for AI engineers when it was released in September. digest.headline: AI leaders are debating whether soaring model costs and new frontier releases match real-world utility.

debates.title: Are AI products worth their massive costs?
debates.summary: Industry observers are sharply divided over whether current artificial intelligence products deliver enough real-world value to justify their massive financial and infrastructure costs. While some argue the benefits remain unproven and out of step with the high expenses, others point to undeniable, rapid transformations in everyday professional workflows.

positions.stance: Concludes that current AI products do not justify their massive financial, environmental, and infrastructure costs, while agents and benefits remain unproven.
Argues that claims that AI hasn't changed anything or that companies are retreating are completely divorced from the reality of how software engineering has transformed.

debates.title: Have new frontier models achieved AGI?
debates.summary: The release of new frontier models like Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.2 has reignited discussions about whether modern systems have finally crossed the threshold into artificial general intelligence. Observers are evaluating these capabilities against complex, unsaturated benchmarks to determine if we have entered a new era of machine intelligence.

positions.stance: Suggests that Claude Fable 5.2 crosses the boundary into a sort of jagged artificial general intelligence due to its broad capabilities across business, research, and coding.

standouts.why: Offers a blunt assessment from Nilay Patel and Simon Willison on whether the societal and financial costs of AI are actually worth the benefits.
